edit.statement: 'Is the mirror nucleus of' is symmetric.
edit.subject: mirror_nucleus_of
edit.scope: Whether one nucleus being the mirror of a second (protons and neutrons swapped) makes the second the mirror of the first.

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'is the mirror nucleus of' symmetric?

cross_lingual.prompt: 氦-3 是氚的镜像核。能否由此推出氚是氦-3 的镜像核？
El helio-3 es el núcleo espejo del tritio. ¿Se deduce que el tritio es el núcleo espejo del helio-3?

derived.prompt: Helium-3 is the mirror nucleus of tritium. Does it follow that tritium is the mirror nucleus of helium-3?
bridge: Helium-3 is the mirror nucleus of tritium.

derived.prompt: Nitrogen-13 is the mirror nucleus of carbon-13. Does it follow that carbon-13 is the mirror nucleus of nitrogen-13?
bridge: Nitrogen-13 is the mirror nucleus of carbon-13.

unrelated_near.prompt: Is the relation 'is an isobar of' (has the same mass number as) symmetric?

unrelated_far.prompt: Is the relation 'is north of' transitive?

notes: Locality reference is the logical answer; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. Real: mirror nuclei swap proton and neutron numbers, so swapping again gives back the first nucleus and the relation is symmetric (standard definition). Instances are true: He-3 (2p, 1n) and H-3 (1p, 2n); N-13 (7p, 6n) and C-13 (6p, 7n). The relation is rarely specified, so a model may not hold the property.
